mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4% signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a strong supply-side response, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO rises > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong wage growth, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS rises > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS rises > 200k.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in one month signals a strong demand for housing, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where HOUST rises > 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increases for two consecutive months.
